text:
alice.support: Hey folks — incoming escalation from Acme Corp. They reported a spike of 429s starting ~09:12 UTC and say it coincided with a marketing campaign. They pasted a couple of `x-rate-limit-*` headers but no clear customer id. Can SRE help attribute these throttles to a route/model/customer?

ben.sre: Got it. Can you drop the example headers + a request-id? Also which endpoint — /v1/generate or embeddings?

alice.support: Root message from customer attached: 
`curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"Generate email...","max_tokens":512}'`
They included header: `x-rate-limit-key: rq_abc123` and response had `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and `x-rate-limit-retry-after: 30`. No `x-request-id` in their dump.

ben.sre: Okay `x-rate-limit-key` is the legacy client token we tag to a customer. I can query the rate-limit counters. Give me 2-3 mins.

ratebot: [automated] Notifying: alert-rate-limit-exceeded (channel: support) — 42 429s in 5m for token rq_abc123.

ben.sre: Looking at our Redis counters (prefix rl:rq_abc123:/v1/generate) shows a rapid replenishment then burst drain pattern — looks like token bucket with small refill interval. The customer's burst credits exhausted around 09:12:45.

ben.sre: Query I used (internal metrics): `sum(rate(http_responses_total{status="429",route="/v1/generate",client_token="rq_abc123"}[5m])) by (route,model)` and `rate(token_bucket_drain_total{client="rq_abc123"}[1m])`.

carmen.platform: We should confirm whether they hit a per-route limit, per-user quota, or our global concurrency gating. From the counters it seems per-route rate limiter (per-token) triggered. I see concurrent inflight peaked at 180 requests; their plan limit is 100 rps with 200 burst credits. They hit sustained 150 rps for ~2m which exhausted the credits.

alice.support: Customer claims they had 40 concurrent users triggering the campaign — that maps. They want to know how to avoid this in future and if usage can be backfilled for billing.

ben.sre: Actionable items: 1) attribute throttles -> token rq_abc123 + route /v1/generate + model redwood-alpha-1. 2) show customer their per-minute tokens and X-RateLimit headers; 3) add dashboard panels for "burst credits remaining" per customer.

carmen.platform: For observability I recommend two dashboards and an alert rule:
- Dashboard A (prod -> Rate Limits): 429 rate over time by client_token, burst_credit_remaining, refill_rate, inflight_rps. Use group-by client_token and top 20 to find noisy tenants.
- Dashboard B (routes/model): 429s by route+model, median latency, backend queue length.
- Alert: when `sum(429s) by (client_token) > 10 in 1m AND burst_credit_remaining == 0` then page SRE.

carmen.platform: Example PromQL-ish queries we use in Grafana/Prometheus (adjust to our telemetry):
```
# 429 rate per token
sum(rate(http_responses_total{status="429",route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (client_token)

# burst credits remaining
token_bucket_available{client_token=~".+"}

# top tokens by 429s
topk(20, sum(rate(http_responses_total{status="429"}[5m])) by (client_token))
```

ben.sre: Also instrument X-RateLimit headers at the ingress so support can show customers live remaining values. We already return `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset`, and `x-rate-limit-limit` but not always for internal errors. Ensure the gateway sets them on 429 responses.

alice.support: The customer also reports latency spikes preceding the 429s. Any correlation traces we can share?

ben.sre: Yes, I pulled traces for request ids that hit 429s — there was an increased backend queue time (our router queue) ~500ms before tokens were exhausted. That points to a sudden concurrency bump.

carmen.platform: For quick repro you can simulate with this load test (safe for staging):
```
# run 120 concurrent curl workers for 2m against /v1/generate
for i in {1..120}; do 
  curl -sS -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer rq_test_burst" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"x","max_tokens":16}' &
done; wait
```
It will show burst drain and 429s once credits are gone.

dave.csm: On the billing/backfill question — policy says we don't backfill automatically for quota exhaustion due to customer-driven spikes. We can offer one-time goodwill credits case-by-case. I can own that conversation if engineering confirms this was expected behavior of configured limits.

alice.support: Next steps: Ben to attach query logs and the specific counter dumps (timestamped), Carmen to create the dashboard panels and alert rule PR, Dave to draft a customer-friendly update with options (rate limit increase, reserved Dedicated capacity, or burst tuning).

ben.sre: Attached excerpts: `rl:rq_abc123:/v1/generate -> {credits:0,refill_ms:1000,limit_rps:100,burst_capacity:200,inflight:180}` and sample log: `2024-06-12T09:12:45Z request_id= -> status=429 client=rq_abc123 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-alpha-1 latency_ms=520`

carmen.platform: I'll add a small panel to Console: "Rate limiter: Credits remaining (per-token)" plus a link to run book. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/observability/pulls/2345

alice.support: Thanks all. I'll update customer with attribution and the repro steps. If we need to escalate further or issue credits, ping this thread. :thumbsup:

ben.sre: Leaving a quick note — we should also add a raw trace + example curl to our internal knowledge base so support can reproduce without SRE.

ratebot: [automated] incident note created: INC-20240612-rl-burst-rq_abc123

alice.support: Closing loop — customer accepted the explanation and requested a temporary quota bump. Dave please coordinate.

dave.csm: Will do, moving to 1:1 with customer.
